QF.id: AIFM CII Legal Documents and Negotiations_29

question.text: 'Deccan Venture Fund III' has two founding partners: Mr. Vikram Bhat (IC Chair) and Ms. Radhika Iyer (CIO). LPs insist on a 'key-person' clause. What is the STANDARD effect of a key-person clause trigger in a Cat II AIF LPA/IMA?

answer.text: The AIF is automatically wound up and all unrealised investments are distributed in specie.
The manager's management fee is doubled to retain the remaining team.
The commitment (investment) period is automatically suspended until the key-person event is cured or LPs vote to continue, protecting LPs from deployment without the identified key personnel.
SEBI registration of the AIF is automatically cancelled.

explanation.text: The Logic: A key-person clause protects LPs from 'blind-pool' capital being deployed without the specific personnel on whose strength they committed. Triggering event (death, permanent disability, dedication-test breach, cease-to-be-actively-involved) typically SUSPENDS THE COMMITMENT PERIOD — new investments pause — until either the key-person event is cured (replacement approved by LPAC) or LPs vote to continue/terminate. Automatic wind-up, fee-doubling, and SEBI cancellation are not standard mechanisms. The Trap: Automatic wind-up is too drastic and economically destructive. Fee doubling is absurd. SEBI does not automatically cancel registration on a key-person event — it is a private contractual matter. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers key-person mechanics across all categories. XXI-B Portfolio Manager has a weaker 'named-PM' concept because PMS is client-specific. Manager's Pro-Tip: Negotiate a 90-180 day cure window and a clear LPAC vote mechanic (simple majority of independent LPs, by commitment). Ambiguous cure windows are the number-one cause of protracted LP-GP stand-offs in India.
